source.title: Life Cycle Assessment of the charging station GARO LS4
source.method: Climate impact assessed with an LCA methodology inspired by ISO 14025
source.background_data: ICE v3.0, European EF database, Livsmedelsverket
source.note: Publicly published manufacturer LCA. The material distribution below is read from the pie chart 'Material distribution in GARO LS4' on page 1 of the report; the mass totals, lifetime and emission results are quoted from the report text.

product.name: GARO LS4 ground-mounted AC electric-vehicle charging station

published_results.note_material_hotspots: Aluminium and electronic components each account for about 47% of the raw-material and component production emissions.

published_emission_factors_gco2e_per_kg._note: Used only to cross-check the DEFRA-derived factors, never as model input.

allocation_to_components._note: The report publishes mass by MATERIAL, not by component. Splitting each material total across components is this project's assumption, constrained so that the per-family totals reproduce the published distribution exactly. Rubber (0.5%, gaskets and seals) is folded into the plastics family because neither DEFRA nor the design space resolves it separately.

component_family_override._note: The report's 'Copper/Plastic' category is the tethered charging cable. It is split into the model's copper and plastic families so that the recycled-content lever and the USGS copper price can act on the right parts; the combined mass still equals the published 8% category.

component_interfaces._note: Which joint interface each component sits behind: 0 = door/enclosure closure, 1 = internal chassis and module mounting, 2 = cable entry and gland, -1 = no modelled joint. This mapping is an ASSUMPTION.

service_and_lifetime.service_description: GARO states that with proper service an LS4 has an operating lifetime of about 25 years, against the 15-year technical lifetime used as the LCA's functional unit. The service GARO describes includes 10 km of transport per year and replacement of one residual current device (RCD); the report does not state how many discrete service interventions the 25-year figure assumes.
service_and_lifetime.note: Used in this project to anchor Assumptions.reman_life_extension: (25 - 15) / 15 = 0.667. The base ratio is cited to GARO's own report; mapping it onto exactly one modelled remanufacture cycle is this project's assumption, since the source does not specify the intervention count behind the 25-year figure. Provenance: CITED ratio, ASSUMED cycle count.
